summary: Digby Gut station, Nova Scotia: a fog bell from 1915, a light from 1963, and a green skeletal-tower light since 2014; Coast Guard property, closed.

light.characteristic: LFl G 6s (flash 2 s, eclipse 4 s) since 2014 (CCG list); fixed white before 2014 (LF)

structures.note: Housed a mechanical fog bell; the bell was suspended in a gable above the porch. Removed by helicopter in September 2014 (LF; SaltWire).

structures.type: white shed with a red roof and a pole-mounted light
structures.note: Light shown from a pole beside the shed from 1963; the shed was dismantled in 2014 (LF).

structures.type: square skeleton tower, green and white daymark
structures.note: Set on an existing concrete foundation in 2014 (LF; CCG list).

access.note: Coast Guard property. Path down the steep bank runs through private property as a right-of-way; LF says permission should be sought. Grounds and tower closed.

events.note: Mechanical fog bell in a two-storey bell house, built by day labour under M.J. Egan (LF). The 1916 report lists the item for the year to 31 March 1916.
A light joined the bell; displayed from a pole beside a white shed (LF; SaltWire caption).
Fixed white light replaced by a flashing green light on a skeletal steel tower; fog signal discontinued (LF; CCG list).
Bell house removed by Coast Guard helicopter, 24 September 2014 (LF; SaltWire).
Fog signal discontinued in the same change (LF).

keepers.name: John McGrath
keepers.note: Hired to tend the bell for about $185 a year (LF). LF: 'at least 1923'. Not confirmed in the Marine report statements read.

notes_for_editor: The 1901 Victoria Beach light (heritage-listed 2015, deactivated 2015) is a separate station with its own record and story (ca-ns-victoria-beach); this story cross-refers only. Its keepers (James Hinds, S. Haynes) are not on this station's roster. Keeper John McGrath (1915 to at least 1923) comes from LF; the Marine keeper statements read did not show a McGrath at Digby Gut, so the attribution rests on LF alone. Howard McGrath has no dates. The 1921-22 report lists 'Digby Gut, N.S.' among changes and improvements, with 'installation of 4th order lens' in an OCR column that cannot be matched by position; it is not used. The 1916 table is OCR'd in columns: the station name, work, contractor and cost were matched by column position, and the cost (read 1,799 96, i.e. 1,799.96) is not quoted, LF's 'about $1,800' is used instead. Prim Point's first light is dated 1817 by LF (this page) and 1804 by LF (Victoria Beach page); the Prim Point record's conflict stays open for that station's story. The SaltWire article body is paywalled; only the captions were read. The Digby County Courier article cited by LF was not read. The novascotiavacation.ca tourism page (it gives 1963 and 44 ft) was not used: it is generated copy. The record's 'built 1915' is for a bell house, and 'first_lit' is null though the light dates from 1963; both proposed in corrections. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1916 page image (printed p. 45) was read. The Digby Gut row shows the fog bell, a day-labour ditto and M. J. Egan under contractor or foreman, with cost 1,799 96, so the column-position match is confirmed by the image. The 1902 page image (printed p. 59) confirms the Victoria Beach 1901 entry, which the corpus had marked with a question mark. The SaltWire article date is not visible in the cached text, so the source is cited as 2014 with the caption date. The story no longer places the 1901 Victoria Beach light on the same shore as this station; the 1901 report gives only the eastern side of Digby Gut, and LF gives the northern side of the gut for Victoria Beach. The Prim Point position now follows the Coast Guard entry: the western point of the entrance to Annapolis Basin. The right-of-way is described as the road to the bank, as LF says. The story says that LF is the only source read that names keepers here.
